title: Travel Cards
statementMd:
In the evening Polycarp decided to analyze his today's travel expenses on public transport.

The bus system in the capital of Berland is arranged in such a way that each bus runs along the route between two stops. Each bus has no intermediate stops. So each of the buses continuously runs along the route from one stop to the other and back. There is at most one bus running between a pair of stops.

Polycarp made $*n*$ trips on buses. About each trip the stop where he started the trip and the the stop where he finished are known. The trips follow in the chronological order in Polycarp's notes.

It is known that one trip on any bus costs $*a*$ burles. In case when passenger makes a transshipment the cost of trip decreases to $*b*$ burles ($*b* < *a*$). A passenger makes a transshipment if the stop on which he boards the bus coincides with the stop where he left the previous bus. Obviously, the first trip can not be made with transshipment.

For example, if Polycarp made three consecutive trips: "BerBank" ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/70a0795f45d32287dba0eb83fc4a3f470c6e5537.png) "University", "University" ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/70a0795f45d32287dba0eb83fc4a3f470c6e5537.png) "BerMall", "University" ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/70a0795f45d32287dba0eb83fc4a3f470c6e5537.png) "BerBank", then he payed $*a* + *b* + *a* = 2*a* + *b*$ burles. From the BerBank he arrived to the University, where he made transshipment to the other bus and departed to the BerMall. Then he walked to the University and returned to the BerBank by bus.

Also Polycarp can buy no more than $*k*$ travel cards. Each travel card costs $*f*$ burles. The travel card for a single bus route makes free of charge any trip by this route (in both directions). Once purchased, a travel card can be used any number of times in any direction.

What is the smallest amount of money Polycarp could have spent today if he can buy no more than $*k*$ travel cards?

## Input

The first line contains five integers $*n*, *a*, *b*, *k*, *f*$ ($1 ≤ *n* ≤ 300$, $1 ≤ *b* < *a* ≤ 100$, $0 ≤ *k* ≤ 300$, $1 ≤ *f* ≤ 1000$) where:

- $*n*$ — the number of Polycarp trips,
- $*a*$ — the cost of a regualar single trip,
- $*b*$ — the cost of a trip after a transshipment,
- $*k*$ — the maximum number of travel cards Polycarp can buy,
- $*f*$ — the cost of a single travel card.

The following $*n*$ lines describe the trips in the chronological order. Each line contains exactly two different words separated by a single space — the name of the start stop and the name of the finish stop of the trip. All names consist of uppercase and lowercase English letters and have lengths between $1$ to $20$ letters inclusive. Uppercase and lowercase letters should be considered different.

## Output

Print the smallest amount of money Polycarp could have spent today, if he can purchase no more than $*k*$ travel cards.

## Note

In the first example Polycarp can buy travel card for the route "BerBank ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/ecc94b07e73defe233bfe831f3977337706a2d27.png) University" and spend $8$ burles. Note that his second trip "University" ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/70a0795f45d32287dba0eb83fc4a3f470c6e5537.png) "BerMall" was made after transshipment, so for this trip Polycarp payed $3$ burles. So the minimum total sum equals to $8 + 3 = 11$ burles.

In the second example it doesn't make sense to buy travel cards. Note that each of Polycarp trip (except the first) was made with transshipment. So the minimum total sum equals to $2 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 5$ burles.
statementZhMd:
晚上，Polycarp 决定分析他今天乘坐公共交通工具的出行费用。

Berland 首都的公交系统有如下特点：每辆公交车都在两个站点之间的线路上运行，且中间没有其他站点。因此，每辆公交车都会沿着这条线路从一个站点持续运行到另一个站点，再返回。任意一对站点之间至多有一辆公交车运行。

Polycarp 乘坐公交车进行了 $*n*$ 次出行。他知道每次出行的起点站和终点站。这些出行按照时间顺序记录在 Polycarp 的笔记中。

已知乘坐任意一辆公交车出行一次的费用为 $*a*$ burles。如果乘客进行换乘，则本次出行的费用降为 $*b*$ burles（$*b* < *a*$）。如果乘客上车的站点与他乘坐上一辆公交车下车的站点相同，则称其进行了换乘。显然，第一次出行不可能进行换乘。

例如，如果 Polycarp 连续进行了以下三次出行：“BerBank” ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/70a0795f45d32287dba0eb83fc4a3f470c6e5537.png) “University”、“University” ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/70a0795f45d32287dba0eb83fc4a3f470c6e5537.png) “BerMall”、“University” ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/70a0795f45d32287dba0eb83fc4a3f470c6e5537.png) “BerBank”，那么他需要支付 $*a* + *b* + *a* = 2*a* + *b*$ burles。他从 BerBank 到达 University，在那里换乘了另一辆公交车并前往 BerMall。之后，他步行回到 University，再乘坐公交车返回 BerBank。

此外，Polycarp 最多可以购买 $*k*$ 张交通卡。每张交通卡的价格为 $*f*$ burles。某条公交线路的交通卡可以使乘坐该线路的任意次数出行免费（两个方向均可）。交通卡购买后，可以在任意方向上使用任意次数。

如果 Polycarp 最多购买 $*k*$ 张交通卡，那么他今天可能花费的最少金额是多少？

## 输入格式

第一行包含五个整数 $*n*, *a*, *b*, *k*, *f*$（$1 ≤ *n* ≤ 300$, $1 ≤ *b* < *a* ≤ 100$, $0 ≤ *k* ≤ 300$, $1 ≤ *f* ≤ 1000$），其中：

- $*n*$ — Polycarp 出行的次数；
- $*a*$ — 普通单次出行的费用；
- $*b*$ — 换乘后单次出行的费用；
- $*k*$ — Polycarp 最多可以购买的交通卡数量；
- $*f*$ — 一张交通卡的费用。

接下来的 $*n*$ 行按照时间顺序描述这些出行。每行恰好包含两个由一个空格分隔的不同单词，分别表示出发站和到达站的名称。所有名称仅由大小写英文字母组成，长度为 $1$ 到 $20$。大写字母和小写字母视为不同字符。

## 输出格式

输出 Polycarp 今天可能花费的最少金额，已知他最多可以购买 $*k*$ 张交通卡。

## 说明

在第一个样例中，Polycarp 可以购买 BerBank ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/ecc94b07e73defe233bfe831f3977337706a2d27.png) University 线路的交通卡，并花费 $8$ burles。注意，他的第二次出行 “University” ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/70a0795f45d32287dba0eb83fc4a3f470c6e5537.png) “BerMall” 是在换乘后进行的，因此 Polycarp 只需为这次出行支付 $3$ burles。因此，最小总费用为 $8 + 3 = 11$ burles。

在第二个样例中，购买交通卡没有意义。注意，除了第一次出行外，Polycarp 的每次出行都是在换乘后进行的。因此，最小总费用为 $2 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 5$ burles。
